mainTopic: The dating of the two בתי מקדש and the יובל count (משמרות, רב אשי's six uncounted years, 7 years of conquest and 7 of dividing), then the משנה on minimum lambs and instruments in the מקדש
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא showing that only four משמרות came back from בבל, and that the prophets made ידעיה, not יהויריב, the head משמר of the Second בית המקדש. So the ברייתא that compares the two destructions must mean the other details. רב אשי then gives a new answer to why the Second בית המקדש fell on מוצאי שביעית: the six years from the start of building until עזרא came and sanctified the land are not counted for שמיטה. Verses in עזרא and a ברייתא prove the six years. Next the גמרא returns to the ברייתא about 17 יובלות and explains why 14 years were not counted: 7 of conquest and 7 of dividing the land. כלב's ages (40 at the spying, 78 at the ירדן, 85 at the dividing) prove the 7 years of conquest. The 7 years of dividing come either from logic or from the פסוק in יחזקאל. A new משנה then sets minimums in the מקדש: six inspected lambs, two trumpets and nine harps, but only one cymbal. The גמרא asks how six lambs could cover שבת and ראש השנה. It answers that the number refers only to the תמיד, and that the holiday phrase is just a memory aid. This explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Each returning watch drew six lots, and ידעיה stays first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: חרים, פשחור and אימר each took six portions, as ידעיה did. The prophets ruled that even if יהויריב returned, ידעיה would stay the head משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: חרים came and took his share and the share of his fellow watches, six in all. פשחור did the same, and so did אימר. The prophets among them ruled that even if יהויריב, the original head of the watches, came up to ארץ ישראל, ידעיה would not be pushed out of its place. ידעיה would be the main one and יהויריב would come second to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about the four כהונה watches that returned from בבל. It shows that in the Second בית המקדש, ידעיה replaced יהויריב as the leading watch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only four of the original 24 משמרות came back, so each one drew six lots to rebuild a full set of 24. The prophets also fixed the order permanently, with ידעיה first. This undercuts the claim that יהויריב's watch was serving when the Second בית המקדש was destroyed, the way it was at the First.

keyTerms.meaning: The 24 rotating watches of כהנים who served in the בית המקדש in turns
They set up a rule or arrangement
The main or primary one
Secondary, coming after the main one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think יהויריב lost its status as a משמר. It was still a watch, but in the Second בית המקדש it ranked behind ידעיה.

phrases.notes: Harim took his own lot plus five more, so that the four returning watches could fill all 24 spots.

steps.title: The comparison refers to the other details
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that when the ברייתא compares the two destructions, it means the other details, not the watch of יהויריב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the comparison between the two destructions refers to the remaining details.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls back. The ברייתא that compares the two destructions does not mean that every detail, like יהויריב's watch, was the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ידעיה led the watches in the Second בית המקדש, the matching detail about יהויריב cannot apply to the second destruction. So the ברייתא's comparison covers only the other shared details, like both destructions happening on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a signal that the גמרא is backing away from an earlier assumption
On the rest, meaning about the other details

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that compares the two destructions does not match them in every detail. The point about the watch of יהויריב applies only to the First בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the rest.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא's other matching details between the two destructions, not the part about יהויריב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion forced by the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's comparison of the two destructions applies to the other details, not to the watch of יהויריב.

steps.title: רב אשי: the first six years were not counted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the main question: the six years from the building of the Second בית המקדש until עזרא came and sanctified the land were not part of the שמיטה count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: those six years, until עזרא came up and sanctified the land, are not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the main question: how can the Second בית המקדש have been destroyed on מוצאי שביעית when its 420 years divide evenly into שמיטה cycles?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שמיטה cycle only began once עזרא arrived and sanctified the land. The first six years of the Second בית המקדש therefore fall outside the count. Taking them out shifts the cycle so that the destruction lands in the year after שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: Six years
Went up, meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל
Sanctified the land, which started the קדושה of the land and the שמיטה count
Counts, includes in the calculation

steps.whyThisMatters: The שמיטה count depends on the קדושה of the land. It did not start when the בית המקדש was built, only once עזרא sanctified the land.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Those six years
until Ezra came up and sanctified the land
are not counted.
phrases.notes: He means not counted toward the שמיטה cycle, even though they count toward the 420 years the בית המקדש stood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָנָךְ שֵׁית שְׁנֵי עַד דְּסָלֵיק עֶזְרָא וּמְקַדֵּישׁ לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous approach ended by saying the ברייתא's comparison covers only the other details. רב אשי now gives an independent answer to the original question of how the Second בית המקדש could fall on מוצאי שביעית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recalculation: the start of the count is moved later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שמיטה cycle was counted from the moment the Second בית המקדש was built, so the destruction would fall in a שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The count started six years later, when עזרא sanctified the land, so the destruction falls on מוצאי שביעית.

steps.title: Verses showing when the building started and finished
steps.stepSummary: Verses in עזרא show that work on the בית המקדש resumed in the second year of דריוש and was finished in אדר of his sixth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Then the work on the House of God in ירושלים stopped,' meaning until the second year of דריוש. And it is written: 'This House was finished on the third day of the month of אדר, which was the sixth year of the reign of King דריוש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving the timeline behind רב אשי's six years. These verses give the dates when the building started and when it was finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse shows the building resumed in the second year of דריוש. The second shows it was finished in אדר of his sixth year. These dates are the starting point for counting the years until עזרא arrived.

keyTerms.meaning: Stopped (Aramaic)
The work of (Aramaic)

King דריוש of Persia

phrases.english: As it is written: "Then ceased

steps.title: עזרא arrived the following year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא with a verse shows that עזרא came to ירושלים in the fifth month of the seventh year, one year after the building was finished. That completes the six years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught: at that same time in the following year, עזרא went up together with his group of exiles, as it is written: 'He came to ירושלים in the fifth month, which was the seventh year of the king.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by showing when עזרא arrived: one year after the building was finished, in the seventh year of דריוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The building started in the second year of דריוש, and עזרא came in his seventh year. That gives the six-year gap רב אשי described. Only then did עזרא sanctify the land and the שמיטה count begin.

keyTerms.meaning: In the following year
His group of exiles who came with him from בבל
The fifth month, counting from ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: Building began in year 2 of דריוש and עזרא came in year 7. Those six years before עזרא sanctified the land are not counted for שמיטה, which is why the Second בית המקדש fell on מוצאי שביעית.

phrases.english: And a Baraita taught: at that same time in the following year
Ezra went up, and his exiles with him,
as it is written: "And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month,
which was the seventh year of the king."

steps.raayaObject: That עזרא arrived six years after the building of the Second בית המקדש began

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: the count of 17 יובלות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again. Israel counted 17 יובלות, but not from the day they entered the land, because then the dates would not match the פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: Israel counted seventeen יובלות from when they entered the land until they left. But you cannot say they counted from the moment they entered. If they did, the בית המקדש would have been destroyed at the start of a יובל cycle, and then the יובל could not fall in 'the fourteenth year after the city was struck,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a ברייתא it quoted earlier so it can now look closely at its details. This line sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the יובל count did not start when the Jews entered the land. If it had, the dates would not match יחזקאל's vision, which came in a יובל year 14 years after the חורבן. So the first 14 years (7 of conquest and 7 of dividing) must be left out of the count.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא goes back to a source it quoted earlier to discuss it directly
The 50th year, which ends each cycle of seven שמיטות
The בית המקדש was destroyed
'The city was struck,' meaning ירושלים was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean they never counted those early years for anything. It only means the יובל count did not begin until the land was fully conquered and divided.

phrases.notes: יחזקאל 40:1. The 'and so on' stands for the rest of the ברייתא: take off the 7 years of conquest and the 7 years of dividing.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 17 יובלות were not counted from entry into the land, so that the יובל falls 14 years after the חורבן, as in יחזקאל.

steps.title: How do we know the conquest took seven years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the conquest of the land lasted seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The seven years in which they conquered the land: how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that the conquest of ארץ ישראל lasted exactly seven years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's math needs 14 uncounted years. The גמרא now wants proof for the first seven of them, the years of conquest.

keyTerms.meaning: They conquered
'From where do we know this?' A request for a source

phrases.english: The seven that they conquered, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of one part of the ברייתא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the conquest lasted seven years.

steps.title: כלב's words: 40 when sent, 85 now
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts from כלב's words in יהושע: he was 40 when משה sent him to spy out the land, and he is 85 now.
steps.simpleTranslation: As כלב said: 'I was forty years old when משה the servant of ה׳ sent me from קדש ברנע to spy out the land, and now I am today eighty-five years old.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק where כלב tells his age at two points in time. The next step does the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב gives two ages: 40 when he went as a spy, and 85 when he asked for his portion during the dividing of the land. The gap between them is the key to counting the years of conquest.

keyTerms.meaning: To spy out
The place in the מדבר from which the spies were sent

phrases.english: As Caleb said:
'Forty years old was I
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:7 and 10. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: when Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me
from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַתָּה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם בֶּן חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁמוֹנִים״.
phrases.english: and now I am today eighty-five years old.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלב's ages (40 at the spying, 85 at the dividing) are the basis for the calculation.

steps.title: Doing the math: 78 at the ירדן, so 7 years of conquest
steps.stepSummary: The spies were sent in the second year after leaving מצרים. So כלב was 78 when they crossed the ירדן and 85 at the dividing, which shows the conquest took seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master said: in the first year משה made the משכן. In the second year the משכן was set up and he sent the spies. So how old was כלב when they crossed the ירדן? Eighty less two (78). When the land was being divided he said, 'I am eighty-five years old.' So it turns out they conquered for seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a ברייתא about when the spies were sent to work out כלב's age at the crossing of the ירדן. Then it subtracts to get seven years of conquest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spies went out in year 2 of the 40 years in the מדבר. That leaves 38 more years, so כלב was 40 + 38 = 78 when they entered the land. He was 85 when the dividing began, and 85 − 78 = 7 years of conquest.

keyTerms.meaning: The portable sanctuary in the מדבר
The crossing of the ירדן into the land
Less, minus
The family portions of land

steps.whatToRemember: כלב: 40 at the spying, 78 at the ירדן, 85 at the dividing. That gives 7 years of conquest.

steps.title: How do we know the dividing took seven years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that dividing the land also took seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the seven years in which they divided the land: how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks for proof of the second set of seven years, the time spent dividing the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב's ages only cover the years from crossing the ירדן until the dividing began. The ברייתא also needs seven years of dividing to reach 14 uncounted years, so the גמרא asks for a source for that second set.

keyTerms.meaning: They divided the land into portions

phrases.english: And the seven that they divided, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of question as step 7, now about the dividing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that dividing the land took seven years.

steps.title: First answer: as long as the conquest
steps.stepSummary: Since the conquest took seven years, it makes sense that the dividing also took seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: since they conquered for seven years, they divided for seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer based on logic: the dividing matched the length of the conquest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer has no פסוק. It reasons that dividing the land went at the same pace as conquering it, so the seven years of conquest suggest seven years of dividing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want, say.' Brings one of two possible answers

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by building on the result of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dividing matched the conquest in length: seven years.

steps.title: Second answer: only seven fits the פסוק in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: unless the dividing took seven years, the יובל would not fall 'in the fourteenth year after the city was struck.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: because otherwise you would not find the יובל in 'the fourteenth year after the city was struck.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: it works backward from the date in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know there were 7 years of conquest. The date in יחזקאל only works if 14 years in total were left out of the count, so the dividing must have taken the other 7.

keyTerms.meaning: You find

steps.whatToRemember: 7 years of conquest plus 7 years of dividing gives 14 uncounted years. That is what makes the יובל land where יחזקאל says.

steps.title: The minimum number of inspected lambs kept ready
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that at least six lambs, already checked for blemishes, must always be kept in the לשכת הטלאים. More may be added without limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We never keep fewer than six lambs that were checked for blemishes in the Chamber of the Lambs. That is enough for שבת and the יום טוב days of ראש השנה. One may add as many as one wants.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a minimum number of ready-to-use lambs kept in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lambs must be checked in advance, so a supply of kosher animals is always ready. The משנה ties the number six to 'שבת and the ימים טובים of ראש השנה.' The גמרא will soon question how six can be enough for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marked here as מַתְנִי׳)
We do not go below; the minimum is
Lambs
Inspected and found free of blemishes
The Chamber of the Lambs in the מקדש, where checked lambs were kept
And one may add without limit

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One keeps no fewer than six lambs
that have been inspected, in the Chamber of the Lambs,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves away from the years of conquering and dividing the land to the minimums kept in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At least six inspected lambs must always be ready in the לשכת הטלאים, and there is no upper limit.

steps.title: The minimum number of musical instruments in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: there are at least two trumpets and nine harps, and more may be added. There is only ever one cymbal.
steps.simpleTranslation: We never have fewer than two trumpets or fewer than nine harps, and one may add as many as one wants. But the cymbal is played alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to give minimums for the instruments played in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trumpets and harps follow the same pattern as the lambs: there is a minimum and no maximum. The צלצל is different, because only one is used and none are added.

keyTerms.meaning: Trumpets
Harps or lyres
Cymbal
Alone; only one

phrases.english: One does not have fewer than two trumpets,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from lambs to instruments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are at least two חצוצרות and nine כנורות, with no upper limit, but only one צלצל.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה uses one pattern twice: a fixed minimum, with additions allowed. The צלצל is the one exception, since there is always exactly one.

steps.title: Six lambs are not nearly enough for שבת and ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the daily and additional offerings of שבת and ראש השנה need far more than six lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But the daily offerings and the additional offerings add up to many lambs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's number. If six lambs are meant to cover שבת and ראש השנה, that is far too few.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the משנה as saying six lambs cover every offering of those days. But the תמיד alone uses two lambs each day, and the מוספין of these days add many more. So 'six is enough' does not seem to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offerings brought every morning and afternoon
The extra offerings brought on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש
There are many; they add up to a lot

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But the daily offerings and additional offerings are many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the number six given in the משנה in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that six lambs are 'enough for שבת and the ימים טובים of ראש השנה.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Add up the תמידין and מוספין of שבת and ראש השנה and you need well over six lambs, so the stated reason cannot be right as read.

steps.title: The six lambs are only for the daily offering; the holiday phrase is a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא is describing the normal year and only the תמיד. 'שבת and ימים טובים' is just a memory aid. It then begins restating the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is speaking about the general, everyday situation, and only about the daily offerings. What does 'enough for שבת and ימים טובים' mean? It is just a memory aid. This is what he is saying: one does not keep fewer than six lambs...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by reinterpreting the משנה. It then starts to restate the משנה in its corrected sense, and that restatement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six lambs are not meant to cover every holiday offering, only the תמיד during the ordinary year. Two lambs a day for three days makes six. The phrase about שבת and ראש השנה just helps you remember 'three days in a row,' because ראש השנה's two days can sit next to שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He is speaking about the general, ordinary situation
Alone; only
A sign or memory aid
And this is what he means (introduces a restatement)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה says six lambs cover all the offerings of שבת and ראש השנה. After this answer, those holidays only help you remember the number of days, which is three.

phrases.english: The תנא is speaking of the general situation,
phrases.notes: He means the ordinary days of the year, not special holidays.

phrases.english: and he is speaking only about the daily offerings,
and what is meant by 'enough for שבת and for festival days'?
It is merely a memory aid,
phrases.notes: שבת right next to the two days of ראש השנה makes three days in a row. That is the picture to remember.

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:
one keeps no fewer than six lambs

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא בְּעָלְמָא קָאֵי, וְאַתְּמִידִין לְחוֹדֵיהּ קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the scope of the משנה is narrowed to the תמיד in the ordinary year, and the holiday phrase becomes a memory aid.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The six lambs were meant to cover all the offerings of שבת and ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The six lambs cover only the תמיד for three days. 'שבת and ימים טובים' simply helps you remember the number three.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא can keep a משנה's words but change what they refer to. A phrase that looked like a reason turns out to be only a memory aid.
